title: Winter session likely in first week of December; govt may push women's quota bill

ai.summary: The Indian government plans to hold a Winter session of Parliament in early December to push through a constitutional amendment bill that would expand the Lok Sabha to 850 seats, enabling 33% women's reservation ahead of 2029 elections, amid opposition protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list recheck.

facts.claim: Winter session likely to begin in first week of December
facts.quote: The Winter session of Parliament is likely to begin in the first week of December

facts.claim: Government's biggest legislative priority is the women's reservation bill
facts.quote: with the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill emerging as the government's biggest legislative priority amid an increasingly confrontational political atmosphere over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

facts.claim: Bill requires 361 votes in Lok Sabha to pass
facts.quote: The bill requires a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha, or 361 votes in the present 543-member House.

facts.claim: Ruling NDA has 320 members and needs opposition support
facts.quote: The ruling NDA has 320 members and would need the support of opposition parties to cross the threshold.

facts.claim: Opposition parties are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
facts.quote: Opposition parties, which have stepped up their campaign against the SIR and are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, are expected to take their protests to Parliament

facts.claim: Government confident of passing bill with 15-18 vote margin
facts.quote: A senior government functionary on Thursday expressed confidence that the bill would be passed with a margin of 15 to 18 votes.

facts.claim: Monsoon session adjourned sine die since August 13
facts.quote: The Monsoon session was adjourned sine die (for an indefinite period) on August 13 and has remained unprorogued for 94 days

ai.background_note: The government aims to implement 33% women's reservation in Parliament and state legislatures through delimitation linked to the SIR voter list recheck, which has faced opposition protests.
